transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… it’s mostly that I keep checking things. Boxes, lists, drawers in the condo. I’ll look, and then I’ll look again… even though I know I already did. My wife’s usually waiting for me to just leave it alone and go, but I have trouble moving on.
Do you ever have thoughts, images, or urges that come into your mind that you don’t want to have, that bother you or cause you anxiety?

Yes… I suppose so. I get these nagging thoughts that maybe I threw out something important from my old teaching files, or put a tool in the wrong box. I can tell myself it’s probably not the case, but it comes back anyway, and then I can’t quite settle.
When you have these thoughts, do you feel driven to do something, like checking again or repeating an action, to try to reduce the anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?
Yes… I do. I’ll check the same boxes or a drawer again, or go back over a list, even when I know I already looked. It’s hard to just leave it and move on, even with my wife standing there waiting.
How long have you been experiencing these thoughts and checking behaviors, and have they been affecting your daily life or causing you significant distress?

It’s been going on long enough that it’s… gotten in the way, yes. The condo unpacking has taken much longer than it should. I keep feeling like I can’t move on until things are checked enough.

And I’ve put off some of my library tutoring preparation, and even hobbies, because I’m still stuck verifying things. It’s frustrating, though I suppose I try not to make too much of it.
Do these checking behaviors take up a lot of your time — like more than an hour a day — or get in the way of things you need or want to do?

Yes… it does get in the way. I don’t know if I’ve counted the time exactly, but the unpacking at the condo has dragged on much longer than it should. And I’ve been putting off my library tutoring preparation, and some hobbies, because I feel like I can’t move on until things are checked enough.
When you check things again, is it because you feel like something bad might happen if you don’t — like maybe you’ll lose something important or make a mistake that could have serious consequences?

Yes… that’s about it. I’ll get this nagging thought that maybe I threw away something important from my old teaching files, or put a tool I need in the wrong box. I can tell myself it’s probably not true, but it doesn’t really settle. It comes back, and then I feel like I have to look again.

Have you ever had other kinds of troubling thoughts or urges that make you feel like you need to do something to feel better or prevent something bad from happening—like maybe worries about germs, or needing things to feel 'just right'?

Mostly it’s that same kind of thought… that I may have tossed something important from my old teaching files, or put a tool in the wrong box.

I’ll tell myself it’s probably not likely, but it doesn’t really stay settled. It comes back, and then I feel like I need to check again.
Have you ever had intrusive thoughts about things needing to be in a certain order, or worries about something bad happening to you or someone else if you don't do something specific to prevent it?

Not really about order, no. It’s more… I keep getting these thoughts that I may have thrown away something important from my old teaching files, or put a tool I’ll need in the wrong box. Even when I tell myself that’s probably unlikely, it comes back, and I have trouble settling down until I check.
Do the thoughts themselves — like the idea that you might have thrown away something important — upset you or cause you anxiety on their own, even when you’re not checking?

Yes… the thought itself bothers me. It’s not just the checking. It’ll come up that maybe I threw out something from my old teaching files, or put a tool in the wrong box, and even if I tell myself it’s unlikely, it sort of hangs there. Makes it hard to settle.
Have you ever had sudden, repetitive movements or sounds that you can’t control — like blinking, shrugging, or making a noise — that have happened more than once?
No… not that I’ve noticed. I don’t think I’ve had anything like that.
Have you ever had other types of intrusive or unwanted thoughts that aren’t about checking things, but still cause you a lot of worry or discomfort?

No… not really other kinds. It’s mostly the same nagging thought about maybe having thrown away something important from my old teaching files, or putting a tool I’ll need in the wrong box. I know it’s probably unlikely, but it comes back and I have trouble settling.

Have you ever had any troubling thoughts that weren’t about throwing something away or putting something in the wrong place — like fears of getting sick, harming someone, or needing things to feel perfectly aligned?

No… I don’t think so. It’s really just that same thing — worrying I tossed out something from my teaching files, or put a tool somewhere wrong. Even when I know it probably didn’t happen, it comes back and I can’t quite let it go.
Do you ever find yourself counting, repeating certain words, or doing other specific actions to try to reduce the anxiety or make sure things feel right?

Not counting or words, no. It’s more that I’ll check the same boxes, lists, or drawers in the condo again and again before I can let it go. I know I already looked, and my wife is usually waiting for me to stop, but… I still feel like I have to be sure.
Have you ever had difficulty getting rid of or parting with possessions, even if they weren’t valuable or useful, because of a concern that you might need them later?
I’m not sure I’d say that. I mean, I keep some things, like anyone, but I don’t think I have trouble parting with things just because I might need them later.
Have you ever had any intrusive or unwanted thoughts about harming someone else or yourself, even if you wouldn’t actually act on them?

No… not harming anyone, or myself. It’s more those nagging thoughts that I might’ve thrown out something important from my old teaching papers, or put a tool in the wrong box. I know it’s probably not true, but it comes back and I can’t settle.

Have you ever had persistent, unwanted thoughts that come up over and over again, even when you’re not thinking about checking things, or felt that you had to do something over and over because you couldn’t stop yourself, even if it was something small or private?
Mostly it’s the checking. I’ll go back to the same boxes or drawers, or look over a list again, even though I know I already did it. It’s hard to just stop and move on… even when my wife is waiting.

Do you ever feel like things need to be arranged in a certain way, or that something feels wrong unless it's exactly how it should be — like a drawer not closing all the way, or a list that isn't perfectly complete?
I don’t think so, no. I mean, I like things reasonably in order, but I don’t feel like a drawer has to be just so or a list perfect. Not that I’ve noticed.
Have you ever had any other types of intrusive or unwanted thoughts that aren’t about throwing something away or putting something in the wrong place, even if they didn’t happen recently?

Not really outside of that, no. It’s mainly the thought that I might’ve tossed out something important from my old teaching files, or put a tool where I won’t find it. Even when I tell myself that’s probably not the case, it keeps coming back a bit.
